checks.invariant: OpenEvolve library API: the evaluator pickle and wrapper module must not be replaceable or shadowable by another principal between write and load.
checks.result: api.py is not used by the repo glue (run_openevolve.py:49-52 drives the CLI with a file evaluator). In the API, when output_dir is given or cleanup=False, temp_dir stays None (api.py:157-162) and the evaluator pickle, the wrapper module and the initial program are written straight into tempfile.gettempdir() with open(..., 'w') and default umask (api.py:255-259, 329-333, 360-364). The cross-principal problem is different: Evaluator._load_evaluation_function inserts the evaluator file's directory, here the shared temp dir, at sys.path[0] of the controller and of every worker and imports the module from it, caching bytecode under <tempdir>/__pycache__ (evaluator.py:87-98, controller.py:138, process_parallel.py:131). candidates.title: ShinkaEvolve runner unpickles results_dir/bandit_state.pkl on resume, a file the evaluated program can write
candidates.description: When a ShinkaEvolve run is resumed (same results_dir, programs.sqlite with last_iteration > 0) and LLM bandit selection is enabled (framework default 'ucb'), the runner process loads <results_dir>/bandit_state.pkl with pickle.load. Evaluated programs are stored and executed under the same results_dir (<results_dir>/gen_N/main.py) as plain subprocesses, so LLM-generated code can write that file; whatever it pickles is executed inside the runner process at the next resume, after the evaluation job that wrote it has ended or been killed, and on whatever host or account performs the resume. Load failures are swallowed with a warning, so the run continues normally. Scope limits established from source: the load happens once at resume start-up, never periodically; the runner overwrites the file every 5 completed generations and at normal end, so a planted file survives only if it is the last write; the repo glue disables the bandit (llm_dynamic_selection: None) and uses a fresh timestamped directory, so this is reachable with the vendored framework's own defaults or examples, not through baselines/run_baseline.sh. With the local job backend the evaluated program already has the operator's uid and full filesystem access, so the pickle adds a boundary crossing only where the program's writes are otherwise confined to the results tree (the slurm_docker backend with the results directory mounted) or where a results directory is resumed on another host or account.

candidates.title: OpenEvolve places candidate programs in the shared temp dir, which the benchmark evaluators then put first on sys.path
candidates.description: In the repo's OpenEvolve flow every candidate program is written to the system temp directory itself (tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile with no dir, e.g. /tmp/tmpXXXXXXXX.py). The glue evaluator hands that path to the shared scoring harness, and the in-process problem evaluators insert the program's directory at sys.path[0], import the program and call its entry function while that entry is still present. The directory is therefore the world-writable temp dir: any top-level module the program imports that is not already loaded in the scorer process (the evaluator pre-imports numpy and scipy; other stdlib or third-party names are not) is resolved from the temp dir before the standard library and site-packages. Another local user of the host can pre-place files such as /tmp/<module>.py and have them executed as the operator inside the scorer process, which carries the operator's full environment. This needs no cooperation from the LLM beyond importing a common module. CodeEvolve and ShinkaEvolve do not share the problem because they place the program in a private temporary directory or under the results directory.

candidates.title: OpenEvolve library API writes the evaluator module into the shared temp dir and adds that dir to sys.path of controller and workers
candidates.description: run_evolution() uses a private mkdtemp directory only when output_dir is None and cleanup is True. When the caller passes output_dir or cleanup=False and supplies the evaluator as a callable or a code string, the evaluator pickle, the generated wrapper module and the initial program are written straight into tempfile.gettempdir(). The controller's Evaluator and every worker's Evaluator then insert the evaluator file's directory, which is now the world-writable temp dir, at sys.path[0] (never removed) and import the module from there, with its bytecode cache under <tempdir>/__pycache__. Consequences for another local user of the host: (1) any later import of a not-yet-loaded top-level module in the controller or a worker, including modules resolved while unpickling a cloudpickled evaluator and modules imported by evolved programs that the evaluator loads in-process, is resolved from the temp dir first; (2) if that user owns a pre-created <tempdir>/__pycache__, they can swap the cached .pyc of the evaluator module (source mtime and size are readable) before worker processes import it. Either way their code runs as the operator. The files themselves are created with default umask (world-readable) but cannot be replaced by another user in a sticky temp dir, and their names (uuid4 hex) cannot be pre-created; the evaluated program, which has the operator's uid, can overwrite the pickle, but in this flow it already runs in the worker, so that is not a separate escalation. The repo glue does not use this API (it drives the CLI with a file evaluator), so this affects direct users of the vendored library.

ShinkaEvolve eval_hydra.py loads .hydra/config.yaml found by walking up from --results_dir and instantiates evaluate_function._target_ in every evaluation job; a program evaluated earlier can rewrite <results_dir>/.hydra/config.yaml and thereby choose the callable used to score all later programs (evaluation-job process only, hydra launch path only, not used by the repo glue). Passing the evaluation target from the launcher instead of re-reading it from the results tree would remove this.

OpenEvolve Program.from_dict restores artifact_dir and id from checkpoint JSON without validation: get_artifacts reads every regular file in the restored artifact_dir into prompt snapshots (database.py:2664, process_parallel.py:598) and program.id is joined into the save path (database.py:974). Constrain artifact_dir to the checkpoint's artifacts directory and validate ids as UUIDs on load.

OpenEvolve api.py writes the evaluator pickle, wrapper and initial program with default umask into the shared temp dir when temp_dir is None; they are world-readable and the cloudpickled evaluator can embed captured data. Always create a private mkdtemp directory for these files.

All three baselines pass the full operator environment and an unrestricted filesystem to evaluated programs while keeping resumable state (pickles, sqlite, JSON, hydra config) in the same tree; if resume is ever used, keep run state in a directory the evaluation jobs cannot write.
